payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) can mitigate gender bias in predictions by equalizing contexts for masculine and feminine words, thus improving model performance across genders.

claims.text: Counterfactual Data Augmentation (CDA) mitigates contextual biases by equalizing the representation of masculine and feminine words in training data.
CDA can improve model performance by reducing significant discrepancies in predictions between genders, leading to fairer outcomes in applications.
The use of CDA can help prevent biased predictions in knowledge bases, ensuring that information about both genders is equally represented.
